name: Subfield.closure_le
script:
intro K inst s t
have h_main : Subfield.closure s ≤ t ↔ s ⊆ (↑t : Set K) := by
  constructor
  · -- Prove the forward direction: if `Subfield.closure s ≤ t`, then `s ⊆ (↑t : Set K)`
    intro h x hx
    have h₁ : x ∈ Subfield.closure s := by
      apply Subfield.subset_closure
      exact hx
    have h₂ : x ∈ (t : Set K) := by
      -- Since `Subfield.closure s ≤ t`, we can use the fact that `x` is in `Subfield.closure s` to show it is in `t`
      have h₃ : Subfield.closure s ≤ t := h
      exact h₃ h₁
    simpa using h₂
  · -- Prove the backward direction: if `s ⊆ (↑t : Set K)`, then `Subfield.closure s ≤ t`
    intro h x hx
    have h₁ : x ∈ Subfield.closure s := by
      apply Subfield.subset_closure
      exact hx
    have h₂ : x ∈ (t : Set K) := by
      -- Since `s ⊆ (↑t : Set K)`, we can use the fact that `x` is in `Subfield.closure s` to show it is in `t`
      have h₃ : x ∈ s := by simpa using hx
      exact h h₃
    simpa using h₂
exact h_main

name: Nat.descFactorial_of_lt
script:
intro n k hnk
have h₁ : n.descFactorial k = 0 := by
  -- Use the property of descending factorials to show that if n < k, then n.descFactorial k = 0.
  have h₂ : n.descFactorial k = 0 := by
    -- Use the definition of descending factorial and properties of natural numbers.
    rw [Nat.descFactorial_eq_prod_range]
    -- Simplify the product using the fact that n < k.
    have h₃ : ∀ i ∈ Finset.range k, (n + i) > 0 → (n + i) ≠ 0 := by
      intro i hi h_pos
      omega
    have h₄ : ∏ i in Finset.range k, (n + i) = 0 := by
      -- Use the fact that n < k to show that the product is zero.
      have h₅ : n < k := hnk
      have h₆ : n ∈ Finset.range k := by
        simp [Finset.mem_range]
        <;> omega
      have h₇ : (n + n) = 0 → False := by
        intro h
        have h₈ : n + n > 0 := by
          omega
        omega
      have h₈ : ∏ i in Finset.range k, (n + i) = 0 := by
        -- Use the fact that n < k to show that the product is zero.
        apply Finset.prod_eq_zero h₆
        simp_all [Nat.add_assoc]
        <;> omega
      exact h₈
    simp_all [Finset.prod_eq_zero_iff, Nat.add_assoc]
    <;> aesop
  exact h₂
exact h₁

name: Matroid.IsStrictMinor.ne
script:
intro α M N h
have h₁ : M ≤ N := by
  -- Use the given inequality `N <m M` to derive `M ≤ N`
  exact le_of_lt h

have h₂ : ¬(N ≤ M) := by
  -- Assume for contradiction that `N ≤ M`
  intro h₃
  -- If both `M ≤ N` and `N ≤ M`, then `M = N`
  have h₄ : M = N := by
    -- Use the antisymmetry of the order relation to conclude `M = N`
    exact le_antisymm h₁ h₃
  -- Substitute `M = N` into the inequality `N <m M` to get a contradiction
  rw [h₄] at h
  -- Simplify the inequality to show that it leads to a false statement
  simp_all [lt_irrefl]
  <;> aesop

have h₃ : N ≠ M := by
  intro h₄
  -- Assume `N = M` and derive a contradiction.
  apply h₂
  -- Use the assumption `N = M` to show `N ≤ M`.
  rw [h₄]
  <;> exact le_refl M

exact h₃

name: isSelfAdjoint_map
script:
intro F R S inst inst_1 inst_2 inst_3 inst_4 f x
have h₁ : ∀ (r : R), r * = r := by

have h₂ : (f x) * = f (x *) := by
  -- Use the property of StarHomClass to relate the star operation on S with F and R.
  have h₂₁ : ∀ (a : F) (r : R), a * r = a r * := by
    intro a r
    exact inst_3.map_mul a r
  -- Apply the above property to f and x to get (f x) * = f (x *)
  have h₂₂ : (f x) * = f (x *) := by
    calc
      (f x) * = f x * := by simp [h₁]
      _ = f (x *) := by
        -- Use the property of StarHomClass to relate the star operation on S with F and R.
        have h₂₃ : ∀ (a : F) (r : R), a * r = a r * := by
          intro a r
          exact inst_3.map_mul a r
        -- Apply the above property to f and x to get (f x) * = f (x *)
        have h₂₄ : f * x = f x * := by simp [h₁]
        simpa [h₁] using h₂₃ f x
  exact h₂₂

have h₃ : (f x) * = f x := by
  calc
    (f x) * = f (x *) := h₂
    _ = f x := by rw [h₁ x]

  rw [IsSelfAdjoint]

name: Metric.infEDist_eq_top_iff
script:
intro α inst s x
have h_imp : Metric.infEDist x s = ⊤ → s = ∅ := by
  intro h
  by_contra h₁
  -- Assume s is not empty, so there exists some y ∈ s
  have h₂ : s.Nonempty := Set.nonempty_iff_ne_empty.mpr h₁
  obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := h₂
  have h₃ : dist x y < ⊤ := by
    -- The distance from x to y is finite and less than ⊤
    exact lt_of_le (dist_nonneg _) (by simp [top_eq])
  have h₄ : Metric.infEDist x s ≤ dist x y := by
    -- The infimum of distances from x to points in s is at most the distance to y
    apply Metric.inf_edist_le hy
  have h₅ : Metric.infEDist x s < ⊤ := by
    -- Since Metric.infEDist x s ≤ dist x y and dist x y < ⊤, we get Metric.infEDist x s < ⊤
    calc
      Metric.infEDist x s ≤ dist x y := h₄
      _ < ⊤ := h₃
  -- This contradicts the assumption that Metric.infEDist x s = ⊤
  rw [h] at *
  exact absurd h₅ (by simp [top_eq])

have h_conv : s = ∅ → Metric.infEDist x s = ⊤ := by
  intro h
  rw [h]
  -- If s is empty, then the infimum of distances from x to points in s is ⊤
  simp [Metric.infEDist_empty]
  <;>
  aesop

have h_main : Metric.infEDist x s = ⊤ ↔ s = ∅ := by
  constructor
  · -- Prove the forward direction: if Metric.infEDist x s = ⊤, then s = ∅
    intro h
    exact h_imp h
  · -- Prove the backward direction: if s = ∅, then Metric.infEDist x s = ⊤
    intro h
    exact h_conv h

exact h_main

have h_main : (p + q).sum f = p.sum f + q.sum f := by
  -- Prove that the sum of the sums is the sum of the polynomials evaluated at f.
  rw [Polynomial.sum_add_distrib]
  <;>
  simp_all [hf₀, hf₁, add_assoc]
  <;>
  ring_nf
  <;>
  aesop

name: MeasurableSpace.measurableSet_bot_iff
script:
intro α s
have h₁ : MeasurableSet s → s = ∅ ∨ s = Set.univ := by
  intro h
  by_cases h₂ : s = ∅
  · exact Or.inl h₂
  · -- If s ≠ ∅, we need to show that s = univ
    have h₃ : s = Set.univ := by
      -- Use the fact that if a set is measurable and not empty, it must be the whole space
      apply Set.eq_univ_of_forall
      intro x
      have h₄ : MeasurableSet s := h
      have h₅ : x ∈ s ∨ x ∉ s := by by_cases h₆ : x ∈ s <;> [exact Or.inl h₆; exact Or.inr h₆]
      cases h₅ with
      | inl h₅ =>
        -- If x ∈ s, then we are done
        simp_all
      | inr h₅ =>
        -- If x ∉ s, we need to derive a contradiction
        have h₆ : MeasurableSet (sᶜ) := by
          apply MeasurableSet.compl
          exact h
        have h₇ : x ∈ sᶜ := by simpa using h₅
        have h₈ : MeasurableSet s := h
        -- Use the fact that if a set is measurable and its complement is also measurable, then it must be the whole space or empty
        have h₉ : MeasurableSet (s ∩ {x}) := by
          apply MeasurableSet.inter h₈
          exact mea
        have h₁₀ : x ∈ s ∩ {x} ↔ False := by
          constructor <;> intro h₁₀ <;>
            simp_all [Set.mem_inter_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
          <;> aesop
        -- Use the fact that if a set is measurable and its complement is also measurable, then it must be the whole space or empty
        have h₁₁ : MeasurableSet (s ∩ {x}) := by
          apply MeasurableSet.inter h₈
          exact mea
        simp_all [Set.mem_inter_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
        <;> aesop
    exact Or.inr h₃
have h₂ : s = ∅ ∨ s = Set.univ → MeasurableSet s := by
  intro h
  cases h with
  | inl h =>
    rw [h]
    exact measurableSet_empty
  | inr h =>
    rw [h]
    exact measurableSet_univ
exact ⟨h₁, h₂⟩
